Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

habeō

habeō, habēre, habuī, habitum

verb, second conjugation, with prō and the ablative

consider, regard (someone or something as …); have (something) done, found out, settled (cognitum habeō); have

In this lexicon

  • consider

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BG 1.44: sēsē illum nōn prō amīcō, sed prō hoste habitūrum; Cic. Att. 13.1.2: istuc jam prō factō habeō; Traupman 296

  • have

    also used · classical · Sall. Cat. 58.1: compertum ego habeō (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 13.17.3: sī nōndum eum satis habēs cognitum (Lewis & Short)

  • have

    the recommended word · classical · Phaedr. 4.25.16–21: cum opus est, nīl habēs

  • persuāsum habeō: convince

    classical

  • Mē male habeō.: I don’t feel well

    classical

  • Melius mē habeō.: I feel better

    classical

  • Mē bene habeō.: I’m fine

    classical

Examples

    I consider that as good as doneCic. Att. 13.1.2
